newsitem.title: USA: Four Corners 750 MW unit down another 1-3 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Four Corners 750 MW unit down another 1-3 weeks.

text.p: The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico will be down for at least another week and possibly three more weeks, a spokeswoman for the plant said Friday.

The unit had been expected to restart Thursday night, after being shut early Tuesday for unplanned repairs, but new problems related to generator ground repairs led to the outage extension, the spokeswoman said.
Furthermore, output from the plant's 750 MW unit 4 has been cut to 415 MW due to mechanical problems.
An estimate for how long unit 4 will be curtailed was uncertain, the spokeswoman noted.
Four Corners' units 1, 2 and 3, were operating at normal rates of 167 MW, 170 MW and 220 MW, respectively, she said.
Arizona Public Service Co, a unit of Pinnacle West Capital Corp, operates Four Corners and owns 1, 2 and 3 along with 15 percent of units 4 and 5.
Southern California Edison Co, a unit of Edison International, holds a 48 percent stake in units 4 and 5.
